chain.label: Fire of undetermined origin ignites in concealed lower amenities section of aft lavatory and burns hidden behind the liner
chain.trigger: the probable causes of the accident were a fire of undetermined origin

chain.label: No lavatory smoke detector and no full-face smoke mask/oxygen for cabin crew required or installed, despite 1973 Safety Board recommendations
chain.trigger: The lavatories on board Flight 797 were not equipped with smoke detectors nor were they required to be so equipped by either Canadian or United States regulations

chain.label: Three aft-lavatory flush motor circuit breakers trip at 1851:14 from fire-damaged wiring and will not reset
chain.trigger: the three circuit breakers associated with the aft lavatory's flush motor ... tripped in rapid succession

caused_by.evidence: the damage to the wiring which caused the three flush motor circuit breakers to trip was caused by heat and fire

chain.label: Captain attributes the breaker trips to a seized flush motor and orders no inspection of the lavatory
chain.trigger: The captain assumed that the flush motor had probably seized and took no further action at this time

caused_by.evidence: After identifying the circuit breakers, the captain immediately made one attempt to reset them; the circuit breakers would not reset

chain.label: Cabin crew cannot locate or reach the hidden fire: CO2 discharged blind at the wall seams, crash axe not used because the attendant was never trained on which panels could be removed
chain.trigger: he was not taught which lavatory panels could be removed or destroyed without endangering critical airplane components

caused_by.evidence: he observed thick curls of black smoke coming out of the seams of the aft lavatory walls

had an oxygen bottle with a full-face smoke mask been available and used, it might have encouraged and enabled the first attendant to take immediate and aggressive actions to locate the source of the smoke

chain.label: First officer and flight attendant in charge give the captain optimistic 'it's clearing/easing up' reports and never tell him the fire was never located
chain.trigger: the captain didn't 'have to worry, I think its gonna be easing up' ... 'it's starting to clear now'

caused_by.evidence: Since the flight attendant in charge and the first officer were not able to determine the location of the fire, they were not able to assess the severity of the fire

chain.label: Generator feeder cables fault in the heat under the lavatory floor; a.c./d.c. and emergency buses lost, disabling transponder, attitude and heading instruments and stabilizer trim
chain.trigger: the master warning light illuminated and the annunciator lights indicated that the emergency a.c. and d.c. electrical buses had lost power

caused_by.evidence: The hot gases caused the aluminum vent tube to melt away ... As a result of the heat, faults developed on the left and right generator feeder cables, and between 1905:35 and 1907:41, the protective circuits tripped them off the line

chain.label: Captain underestimates fire severity and delays the emergency descent about 5 1/2 minutes after being told of the fire
chain.trigger: about 5 minutes 30 seconds elapsed between the time that the No. 2 flight attendant told the captain there was a fire in the aft lavatory and his decision to begin the emergency descent

caused_by.evidence: misleading fire progress information provided to the captain
In retrospect, his decision not to do so may have forestalled an early opportunity to discover the fire

chain.label: Faulty interfacility handoff: Cincinnati approach mistakes Continental 383's beacon target for Flight 797 (Board found no appreciable landing delay)
chain.trigger: he had mistaken the radar beacon target of Continental Flight 383 as that of Flight 797

caused_by.evidence: Since Flight 797's transponder was inoperative, an automated handoff of the flight from Indianapolis Center to the Cincinnati TRACON was not possible

chain.label: First officer switches the air conditioning packs off, ending all cabin air exchange for the last 4+ minutes; smoke, heat and combustible gases accumulate unpurged and visibility drops to nil above 1 foot
chain.trigger: although it is not required by the emergency procedure checklist, he turned the air conditioning and pressurization packs off ... he thought the packs were feeding the fire

caused_by.evidence: because the smoke was getting bad at that point and my reasoning was I have to do something
with the loss of electrical power, the augmentation valve in the pressurization system closed, and high pressure bleed air was not available

chain.label: Emergency landing on runway 27L at Greater Cincinnati at 1920:09, roughly 3 to 5 minutes later than an earlier descent to Standiford Field would have allowed
chain.trigger: At 1920:09, eastern daylight time, Flight 797 landed on runway 27L at the Greater Cincinnati International Airport

caused_by.evidence: the only factor which significantly delayed Flight 797's landing was the flightcrew's delayed decision to descend

chain.label: Flash fire engulfs the cabin 60-90 seconds after the exits are opened; 23 passengers die, 3 seriously injured, airplane destroyed
chain.trigger: About 60 to 90 seconds after the exits were opened, a flash fire enveloped the airplane interior ... 23 passengers were not able to get out of the plane and died in the fire

caused_by.evidence: both forward exit doors and three overwing emergency exit windows were opened and an unlimited supply of fresh oxygen became available to the fire ... a back draft and flashfire occurred
with no airflow available to reduce the buildup of heat and combustible gases at the upper levels of the cabin, the onset of factors conducive to flashover or flashfire was accelerated

the decreased exposure time of the passengers to the toxic environment in the cabin would have enhanced their physical and psychological capability to escape ... the delayed decision to descend contributed to the severity of the accident
